meta.topic: Holding mail while away (national postal hold services), house- and pet-sitter prices, and published figures on burglary of empty or occupied homes
markets: US: New York City, Los Angeles, New Haven CT

mailHold.priceText: USPS Hold Mail® Service is a free service
mailHold.advanceBookingText: You can enter an online USPS Hold Mail request up to 30 days in advance of the start date or as early as the next scheduled delivery day.
mailHold.sameDayCutoff: Request your Hold Mail service start date by 3 AM ET (2 AM CT or 12 AM PT) on your requested day, Monday-Saturday.
atEnd: Option A: carrier delivers the accumulated mail on the last day of the hold.
Option B: collect the accumulated mail at the local Post Office; it must be picked up within 10 days or it is returned to the senders.
mailHold.longerThanMax: For longer than 30 days USPS directs customers to a forwarding service.
mailHold.note: Free, minimum 3 / maximum 30 days, 30-day advance window, and both end options were all read on USPS's own pages (FAQ article and usps.com/manage/hold-mail.htm).

prices.duration: each additional name (beyond the 4 included, up to 4 more)

mailHold.minimumBasis: The minimum residential rate is based on a 10-weekday period (weekdays include statutory holidays); it can be bought for a shorter period at the same minimum rate.
mailHold.startLead: Service typically begins 3 business days after you place your order.
mailHold.maxDuration: No maximum stated on the product page or the HTML terms page; the service can be extended.
mailHold.atEnd: On the next business day following the expiry or cancellation date, Canada Post will deliver the mail held for your address.
mailHold.duringHold: During the Hold Mail period, mail pickup is not available at any Canada Post location.
mailHold.notHeld: Parcels (Priority, Xpresspost, Xpresspost Certified, Expedited Parcel, Regular Parcel) and prepaid envelopes may be delivered during the hold; newspapers and flyers are not held; no hold for shared postal addresses, institutions or FlexDelivery addresses.
mailHold.refunds: No refunds are provided once the service has started.
mailHold.note: Prices, 3-business-day start, delivery the next business day after expiry, no pickup during hold and no refunds were all read on Canada Post's own pages.

prices.duration: each additional individual name (up to 4 more)

mailHold.note: Read on Canada Post's own page. Included for completeness; the player household uses the residential rate.

mailHold.noticeText: At least 5 working days before the start date (third-party guide).
mailHold.atEnd: Third-party guide: on the chosen end date Royal Mail delivers all held mail together on the next working day; a large volume may come as a collection card for the local delivery office (18 days to collect).
mailHold.note: royalmail.com returned HTTP 403 to every fetch (product page, prices2026, the April 2026 price-guide PDFs). The prices above come from web-search summaries of Royal Mail's April 2026 price guides and of mailcoms.co.uk (£27.50 for 17 days, £34 for 24, £42 for 31, £78 for 66, £114.50 for 100). postofficehours.co.uk gives different, rounded figures ('~£18 / 10 days, ~£28 / 17, ~£39 / 24, ~£49 / 31, ~£70 / 66, ~£90 / 100') and tells readers to confirm them on royalmail.com, so its figures are not used here. October 2024 figures quoted in search: £23.50 for 17 days, £67 for 66 days. There was no price for a 10-day band. The notice period and end-of-hold handling are from postofficehours.co.uk and are unconfirmed. A 100-day maximum also appears on franking-machine-warehouse.co.uk.

mailHold.note: Read on a reseller's page (franking-machine-warehouse.co.uk), not on royalmail.com, which returned 403. The £110 / 100-day figure comes only from a search summary. Prices are VAT-exempt.

mailHold.maxText: The maximum amount of time you can take out the Service for is twelve weeks.
mailHold.atEnd: Mail is stored safely and delivered when you return; delivery resumes on the return date the customer gives.
mailHold.notHeld: Does not apply to items sent via the An Post parcel service.
mailHold.note: Read on An Post's own page. Applications must be in at least 5 working days before the start date.

mailHold.service: Correos de México Almacenaje (storage of items at the post office)
mailHold.maxText: Up to 20 working days, counted from the sixteenth working day after the item reaches the post office (one summary says from the eleventh day).
mailHold.atEnd: The item is collected by the addressee at the post office.
mailHold.note: No home-delivery hold equivalent to USPS / Canada Post / Royal Mail / An Post was found for Correos de México. The nearest service is 'Almacenaje', which keeps correspondence and shipments at the post office on request from the sender or addressee. Its description comes from search summaries of Correos de México's own procedures manual (CO2.pdf, which refused the connection: ECONNREFUSED) and of a Correos de México post on X ('guarda tus envíos hasta por 20 días hábiles'). There was no price. It stores items awaiting collection at the office. It does not suspend delivery to the home.

awayBurglary.figure: In over half of incidents of domestic burglary in a dwelling where an offender gained entry into the dwelling, someone was at home at the time.
awayBurglary.period: Crime Survey for England and Wales, year ending March 2017
otherFigures: Around 70% of domestic burglaries in dwellings take place during the week (16% per weekday) and around 30% at the weekend (12% per weekend day).
Approximately two-fifths take place 6am-6pm and three-fifths 6pm-6am.
awayBurglary.note: Read on ONS's own article (released 20 July 2017). It has no figure for holidays or absence, or for signs such as uncollected post. ONS points to its 'Nature of Crime' tables for more circumstantial detail, which were not read. Search summaries also quote 58% and 68.9% 'someone home' figures, from other years or with attempts included. Those were not traced to an ONS page.

awayBurglary.figure: Household burglary when someone was home: 9 per 1,000 households in 2000 and 8 per 1,000 in 2007 (stable). About 7% (266,560) of burglaries involved violent victimization. An estimated 3.7 million burglaries a year on average, 2003-2007.
awayBurglary.note: The rates, the 7% and the 3.7 million were read on BJS's own pages (press release and publication page, BJS Special Report, September 2010). The '28%' (about 1 million of 3.7 million with a household member present) comes only from search summaries of the report PDF, whose text could not be extracted. Treat the 28% as confirmed: false.

awayBurglary.figure: More than half of those surveyed leave their home empty when gone for three days or longer. Of those who do, only 41% lock all doors that give access to the home and only 35% lock all windows. Three in ten never post on social media while away on holiday. Nearly a quarter are more anxious about burglary in the peak summer holiday season, and Christmas is the top worry period (32%). One in five believe leaving a property unoccupied beyond the policy's day limit would not invalidate a claim, and a further 30% are unsure.
awayBurglary.sample: Censuswide for Aviva (J15666CWMPB), 2,000 UK nationally representative consumers, 5-7 January 2026
awayBurglary.note: Read on Aviva's own page. It is an attitude and behaviour survey. It does NOT measure how often empty homes are burgled. It is relevant to the unoccupancy clauses in insurance policies.
